newsitem.title: GERMANY: SANTER SAYS EMU RULES SHOULD BE STRICTLY APPLIED.
newsitem.headline: SANTER SAYS EMU RULES SHOULD BE STRICTLY APPLIED.

text.p: Entrance criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) should be strictly applied in order to create a solid single currency, European Commission President Jacques Santer told a German magazine, according to an advance text issued on Wednesday.
"We must interpret the entry criteria restrictively so that the euro wins credibility in the finance markets," Santer said in an interview to appear in Thursday's issue of Wirtschafts Woche.
He also said political posturing was complicating the EMU launch, and that reforming European Union political bodies was critical for EMU and the union's expansion into eastern Europe.

"In all member states, politicians are talking about what the governments in neighbor states are doing or not doing," he said. "Instead, each should worry about his own budget and work to reach the goals set out in the Maastricht Treaty."

A failure to reform EU political institutions -- a key topic for the June EU summit in Amsterdam -- would result in "negative psychological effects" and "poison the atmosphere" for a single currency, he said.

In addition, an EU without political reform would only become more difficult to manage with Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic and other former Soviet bloc states increasing the member count, he said.
